question.text: Which is true about Buna-<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>?

options.text: It is a linear polymer of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></math>-butadiene.
It is obtained by copolymerization of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></math> -butadiene and styrene.
It is obtained by copolymerization of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></math> -butadiene and acrylonitrile.

The suffix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> in Buna- <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> stands for its natural occurrence.

solution.text:
Buna-N is formed by the co-polymerization of 1,3-butadiene and vinylcyanide(acrylonitrile) in the presence of a peroxide catalyst.

It is a synthetic rubber.
